title: Sandbox quickloops + rescue manual (draft)
body:
Overview:
This working note defines a small set of lightweight SDK "quickloops" (short runnable walkthroughs) plus a compact rescue manual that we will inline with each example. Aim: make a new engineer or solutions lead reach a meaningful demo in under 30 minutes and provide deterministic steps to recover from the top failure modes.

High-level goals:
- 3 minimal, language-agnostic quickloops: generator, chat+function, embeddings search
- Each quickloop = one page, one runnable command, one smoke test, and telemetry hooks
- Include an explicit rescue section at the top of every doc with 5 prioritized checks

Design constraints and non-goals:
- Keep dependencies tiny (standard library + single third-party dep where unavoidable)
- Do not require cloud credentials; use sandbox tokens and local mock HTTP for the platform API
- Not meant to be exhaustive tutorials; these are first-run proofs to encourage further exploration

Quickloop outlines (short):
1) Text generator quickloop
  - TL;DR: run a single command that posts a prompt and prints a streaming response
  - Languages: Python + Node examples included
  - Key points to show: streaming vs non-streaming, model fallback option, expected stdout sample
  - Run command example: `SANDBOX_TOKEN=... ./run-gen.sh`
2) Chat with function-calling quickloop
  - TL;DR: small web UI + server that demonstrates a model invoking a function schema; validator script confirms payload shape
  - Key points: function schema, response parsing, simple retry when validation fails
  - Run command example: `docker-compose up --build`
  - Expected outputs: console log lines showing function call, validated payload, and final response
3) Embeddings + similarity quickloop
  - TL;DR: index 10 short docs, run a similarity query, print top-3 results with distances
  - Key points: cost/latency note, local in-memory index for reproducibility, fuzz-tolerant assertions for CI
  - Run command example: `python examples/embed_search.py --token $SANDBOX`

Snackable format (must be followed for each quickloop):
- Title (single sentence)
- TL;DR (1 line run command + 1-sentence outcome)
- Why it matters (2 bullets)
- Prereqs (OS, deps, token)
- Steps (explicit numbered commands; include expected output snippets)
- Rescue checklist (top 5)
- Minimal telemetry contract to emit and how to assert in CI
- Quick troubleshooting (3-6 fixes)
- Next links and related longer examples

Rescue checklist (to appear at top of each quickloop):
1) Confirm token presence and format: `echo $SANDBOX_TOKEN` and check for expected prefix (sandbox_ or test_)
2) Validate network route: `curl -v --max-time 3 $SANDBOX_API/ping`
3) Enable debug logs: set `DEBUG=redwood*` and repeat the run to capture request_id
4) If streaming stalls: re-run with `--no-stream` to get non-chunked response and capture verbose timing
5) Swap to tiny fallback model: set `MODEL=tiny-test-1` and re-run to determine if issue is model-size related

Common errors and quick responses:
- Auth failure: rotate sandbox token, ensure env var exported in shell session, check account in console (link in header)
- Timeout: reduce max_tokens, increase client timeout, or route to local mock API for reproducible debugging
- Schema/function call failure: run included validator script which reports missing/extra fields; return a 200 with `{"ok":false, "errors":[...]}` for local debugging

Telemetry minimal contract:
- Events emitted by each example: on_start, on_success, on_error, duration_ms, model_name, variant
- CI assertion: example run should produce on_success and duration_ms < 2000ms for generator quickloop (configurable)
- Telemetry sink: lightweight HTTP endpoint stub we include in examples that validates event shape during CI runs

CI smoke tests (examples):
- `onboard-smoke-gen`: run generator quickloop, assert stdout snapshots fuzzy-match and telemetry on_success present
- `onboard-smoke-chat`: start containerized app, curl health endpoint, POST sample chat, assert function-call payload validated
- `onboard-smoke-embed`: run embed + search CLI; assert results contain expected doc ids within top-3

Implementation plan (2 sprints, pragmatic):
Sprint A (week 1):
- Day 1: sprint kickoff, pick owners, create example repo skeleton, add telemetry stub
- Day 2-4: implement generator + embeddings quickloops and baseline smoke tests
- Day 5: pair review, update rescue checklist, green smoke tests locally
Sprint B (week 2):
- Day 1-3: implement chat+function quickloop, validator script, and web client minimal UI
- Day 4: CI wiring, adjust telemetry assertions, create PRs and address review comments
- Day 5: publish drafts to docs review channel and tag for next docs sprint

Roles and owners (short strings):
- content_owner: Aisha Patel
- examples_engineer: Marco Chen
- devrel_reviewer: Lena Ortiz
- ci_telemetry_owner: Ravi Singh

Acceptance criteria (per quickloop):
- Single command runs end-to-end in <10 minutes with sandbox token
- Smoke CI job passes in <5 minutes and emits on_success event
- Rescue checklist visible at top of doc and validated in PR review
- No secrets or production credentials required to run

Open questions (to triage in kickoff):
- Single shared telemetry sink vs per-team dev sinks?
- Standard fallback model names to use across examples
- Naming scheme for repo/examples (prefixes?)

Next actions (immediate):
- Create repo skeleton: examples/onboard-quickloops (assign Marco)
- Add telemetry stub and CI job (assign Ravi)
- Author Python and Node generator quickloops (Aisha + Marco)
- Sync with DevRel on TL;DR messaging (Lena)

History notes:
- 2025-02-14: created by Aisha (initial outline)
- 2025-02-21: added telemetry contract and CI sketches (Ravi)
- 2025-03-02: integrated smoke tests and owners (Marco)

Feedback instructions:
This is a draft. Please leave line comments in the PR or add inline suggestions in the Drive doc. Prefer concrete examples that run locally without cloud infra.
